key_insight: Healthcare LLMs can look highly accurate on clean questions yet still fail badly when they must decide whether to answer, ask for clarification, abstain, or escalate under workflow uncertainty.
clinical_relevance: In patient-facing workflows, unreliable escalation can miss important safety triggers, so decision policies need evaluation beyond answer accuracy alone.
method: 400 synthetic healthcare workflow episodes built from 40 semantic seeds
Five controlled variants tested across four task classes and two surface forms
Compared five open-weight LLM configurations under ANSWER/ASK CLARIFICATION/ABSTAIN/ESCALATE with a preset 5:1 missed-vs-unnecessary escalation cost
evidence_signal: Clean decision accuracy reached 0.97, but uncertainty-prompted models missed 32% to 97% of required escalations and one model fell from 0.97 clean accuracy to 0.78 under conflict.
watch_item: The workflow-aware controller improved benchmark utility, but its rule detectors collapsed on paraphrased triggers, so real-world generalization remains unproven.
paper_title: Auditing Escalation Reliability in Healthcare LLM Agents: A Perturbation-Controlled Benchmark of Workflow-State Failures
